flow.common.activation.tip: gh-aw job: renders the prompt, sanitizes event text, applies the credit guardrail. Rung 2.
flow.ghaw.issue.tip: The trigger. Any GitHub event can start a workflow; here, a label on an Issue.
flow.ghaw.md.tip: The whole workflow in one file: settings on top, the prompt in plain words below.
flow.ghaw.compile.tip: Checks the schema, pins the actions and writes the lock file you commit.
flow.ghaw.actions.tip: A normal GitHub Actions run of that lock file. Nothing special yet.
flow.ghaw.agent.tip: The model runs your prompt inside gh-aw: sandboxed, read-only, behind a firewall, no credentials.
flow.ghaw.safe.tip: A separate job scans the proposal and applies only the writes you declared.
flow.ghaw.pr.tip: The only write this workflow can make: one pull request per run.
flow.router.event.tip: Every trigger the repository has arrives here, as one GitHub event.
flow.router.classify.tip: Pure shell: turns one event into one route. No network, no model. Rung 1.
flow.router.authorize.tip: Checks the sender: write access and org membership, or the bot-working label. Rung 1.
flow.router.route.tip: Dispatches at most one worker, through workflow_call.
flow.router.idle.tip: No permission, or nothing to do: every job is skipped in about ten seconds.
flow.router.deterministic.tip: Cron and manual runs go to plain jobs. No model runs in them.
flow.router.triage.tip: The front door for people with read-only access.
flow.router.refine.tip: Sizes the work and writes the story. Splits anything of eight points or more.
flow.router.implement.tip: Writes the code and opens one pull request, then stops.
flow.router.gate.tip: The only worker that merges. One at a time for the whole repository.
flow.router.review.tip: Applies the review comments on a bot pull request.
flow.router.audit.tip: Reads the repository every week, read-only, and files one Issue.
flow.router.release.tip: Starts by hand. The agent writes the notes; shell does version and tag.
flow.triage.outside.tip: Triage is only for people without write access. Anyone with write skips it.
flow.triage.idle.tip: A person with write access skips triage: nothing to do, the run ends.
flow.triage.open.tip: Our job still_open: a run can queue 10 minutes, and the Issue may be closed by then. Rung 4.
flow.triage.agent.tip: Our prompt, run in the gh-aw sandbox: ten checks, from template to product scope. Rung 5.
flow.triage.safe.tip: Staged: it writes nothing. Our conclude job applies the result with the App token. Rung 6.
flow.triage.valid.tip: Our validate_output job checks the verdict is one of the four allowed outcomes.
flow.triage.incomplete.tip: Invalid or empty verdict: that is not a decision, so the run is retried.
flow.triage.passed.tip: Adds the refine label. No human involved.
flow.triage.info.tip: Posts questions to the author. A reply re-runs the worker, up to three rounds.
flow.triage.maintainer.tip: Valid, but outside what the bot does. The Issue stays open with a review label.
flow.triage.blocked.tip: A genuine rejection: the Issue is closed and the bot does not retry it.
flow.refine.guard.tip: Our job size_guard: a huge Issue dies mid-generation, so it is measured first. Rung 4.
flow.refine.toobig.tip: Our refuse_big_issue job: comments and parks it, zero tokens. A reply re-runs refine.
flow.refine.explore.tip: Our prompt: reads the real code one work unit at a time, answering its own questions. Rung 5.
flow.refine.trivial.tip: Trivial means 1 to 3 files of style or text, with no logic, data or security.
flow.refine.plan.tip: A small plan with no Gherkin: enough for a style or text change.
flow.refine.story.tip: A user story in Given / When / Then, grounded in the code.
flow.refine.wrap.tip: Puts the story into the Issue form.
flow.refine.prose.tip: Passes the text through the humanizer skill.
flow.refine.estimate.tip: Fibonacci points against fixed bands, from one day to eight or more.
flow.refine.eight.tip: Eight points or more is too big: it is split into 2 to 6 children.
flow.refine.questions.tip: Open questions go to the author in one batched comment.
flow.refine.incomplete.tip: The agent could not ground the story in the code. The run is retried.
flow.refine.refined.tip: Nothing open: the Issue gets the implement label.
flow.refine.asked.tip: One comment with every open question. The reply re-runs refine.
flow.refine.split.tip: Child Issues of five points or less. Each one walks the pipeline alone.
flow.implement.route.tip: The router sends the Issue here when it gets the implement label.
flow.implement.eligible.tip: Our job: the Issue is open and not marked future. Rung 4.
flow.implement.idle.tip: Closed, or marked future: there is nothing to build.
flow.implement.branch.tip: Our content in gh-aw's steps block: it cuts the feature branch before the model runs.
flow.implement.marker.tip: Refine can mark a change trivial. Then our prompt skips the full pipeline.
flow.implement.direct.tip: Trivial path: one todo per item, no plan.
flow.implement.standard.tip: Runs the plan-goal skill: explore, propose, apply, archive.
flow.implement.verify.tip: Runs the project checks on the final files. A failure goes back to the agent.
flow.implement.pr.tip: gh-aw safe output, not staged here: opens one pull request.
flow.implement.handed.tip: Implement stops here. The merge decision belongs to the merge gate.
flow.implement.died.tip: Dying fast, in under six minutes, is an outage. Dying later is a real problem.
flow.implement.retry.tip: A provider or runner outage: the worker retries, up to five attempts.
flow.implement.parked.tip: Something is wrong: the Issue gets a review label for a person.
flow.gate.route.tip: The router calls the gate when CI finishes on a pull request, or to reconcile.
flow.gate.subject.tip: Our job subject: finds the pull request, its Issue and the CI verdict. Rung 4.
flow.gate.idle.tip: Not our pull request, or already closed: nothing to do.
flow.gate.checkout.tip: Our step: checks out the PR branch, fast-forward only.
flow.gate.ci.tip: The router passes the CI conclusion in. There is no polling.
flow.gate.repair.tip: Our prompt: CI is red, so it fixes and verifies, then pushes.
flow.gate.pushed.tip: The push starts CI again, and the gate runs again when it ends.
flow.gate.protected.tip: Our job protected_changes: the blast radius, from paths, CODEOWNERS and size. Rung 4b.
flow.gate.owner.tip: Protected paths need the owner named in CODEOWNERS.
flow.gate.agent.tip: Our prompt: CI is green, so it hunts defects and checks them. It does not decide. Rung 5.
flow.gate.disposition.tip: Shell computes the verdict from the agent report and the blast radius.
flow.gate.automerge.tip: Our conclude job merges with the App token, so CI runs. Only this worker merges.
flow.gate.human.tip: A fragile change or a high radius: parked for a person.
flow.gate.blocked.tip: CI is still red at the sixth attempt: the gate stops.
flow.legend.post: Job after the agent · Safe Outputs
flow.gate.subject: Subject
board.quote.name: Uncle Bob Martin
board.quote.text:
Software engineers are supposed to do exactly what we’ve always done.
Ensure that the composition and structure of the system is robust and
maintainable and that the behavior of the system properly serves the
needs of our users.

This requires engineering discipline. It need not require detailed
reading of the code; just as using compilers does not require detailed
reading of the binary.

talk.workflows.ladder: Rung: lower is cheaper and more repeatable. Shell is 1, agent 5.
talk.health.dora: DORA: DevOps Research and Assessment, a Google Cloud program.
talk.closing.talk: Slides: platform.ckgrafico.com · All open source. Questions?
talk.label.author: Issue author
talk.maturity.line: No AI → Exploratory → Structured → Scaled → Governed & Optimized
talk.sponsors.title: Thank you to our sponsors.
talk.ghaw.title:
GitHub Agentic Workflows
in 5 minutes.
talk.ghaw.body: A workflow is a Markdown file that compiles to Actions. The agent runs sandboxed, read-only, and only proposes. gh-aw scans the proposal, then writes.
talk.local.title:
Understanding it takes 5 minutes.
Getting the bases and the way of
working right took us months.
talk.local.body: So let's talk about it: how we built Platform.
talk.evolution.timeline.title: The evolution of AI.
talk.maturity.levels.title:
We measure different
levels of maturity.
talk.maturity.levels.body: Different teams and companies are at different points in adopting AI across the software development lifecycle.
talk.platform.pillars.title:
The 4 pillars
of Platform.
talk.foundations.conventions.title:
Foundations:
technology conventions.
talk.foundations.conventions.body: A thin base for many apps: a .NET backend, a Next.js frontend and one shared brand. People and agents follow the same rules.
talk.harness.conventions.title:
agent-harness:
agentic conventions.
talk.harness.conventions.body: One command installs it in each repo: OpenSpec for changes, plugins that block unsafe actions, the skills each project needs, and guardrails.
talk.harness.skills.title: An agent is a set of skills.
talk.harness.skills.body: Skills come from skills.sh or from us: global and project guardrails, and Plain conventions. Each agent loads only the skills its work needs.
talk.harness.tiers.title:
Three models per agent:
plan, build and fast.
talk.harness.tiers.body: When it plans, the harness gives each OpenSpec task an agent and a tier. Then it runs the tasks in parallel waves, each on its own files.
talk.workflows.intro.title:
agentic-workflows: asynchronous
development in the cloud.
talk.workflows.intro.body: Our layer on top of GitHub Agentic Workflows: one router, workers that use the agent-harness skills, OpenCode through Forge, and writes only through Safe Outputs.
talk.workflows.router.title: One router for every event.
talk.workflows.router.body: One event, one run, at most one worker. Classification is pure shell with no network calls. An idle run costs about ten seconds.
talk.workflows.triage.title: Triage: the front door.
talk.workflows.triage.body: Four outcomes: pass, needs info, needs a maintainer, block. Three rounds at most. In round three, needs info is no longer allowed.
talk.workflows.refine.title: Refine: size and split the work.
talk.workflows.refine.body: Explore the code one unit at a time. Write the story as Given, When, Then. Estimate in Fibonacci. Eight or more splits into 2 to 6 children.
talk.workflows.implement.title: Implement: one PR, then stop.
talk.workflows.implement.body: Eligible? Reserve, collect facts. Trivial marker takes the direct path, the rest runs plan-goal. Verify the scoped files. One PR. The gate decides.
talk.workflows.gate.title: Merge Gate: the only one that merges.
talk.workflows.gate.body: CI red? Repair, push, CI again. CI green? Measure the blast radius, the agent hunts defects, shell computes the verdict: merge, human, owner or blocked.
talk.workflows.others.title: And four more workers.
talk.workflows.others.body: Apply Review applies review comments on bot PRs. Audit reads the repo weekly and files one Issue. Release writes the notes. Visual Verify takes screenshots after an auto-merge.
talk.health.intro.title:
project-health:
measure the system.
talk.health.intro.body: It reads GitHub every night and changes nothing. Each project has four tabs: Engineering, Delivery, Agentic and Roadmap.
talk.health.engineering.title:
Engineering: the quality
of our code.
talk.health.engineering.body: The practices Platform asks for on the default branch: tests, mutation, security, complexity and code hygiene. In which mode, and if they last passed.
talk.health.delivery.title: Delivery: DORA metrics.
talk.health.delivery.body: How often we ship, how long a change takes to reach production, and how much is rework. GitHub gives three of the five metrics.
talk.health.agentic.title:
Agentic: how far this project
adopts our agents.
talk.health.agentic.body: Measured against our Platform standard: versions, installed workers, and how much merges with no person. Not every project needs the same level.
talk.health.roadmap.title:
Roadmap: from opened
to merged.
talk.health.roadmap.body: How each Issue moved from opened to merged, what happened on the way, and how long it took. Here an agent worked 4% of the open time.
talk.closing.question.title: What exactly are software engineers supposed to do?
talk.system.title:
From Issue to production
with GitHub Agentic Workflows.
talk.system.body: Product experts who do not code file small eligible Issues or bugs. They reach production without human supervision.
